data.title: The NBA bans certain types of parlay bets with its sportsbook partners
data.description:
The NBA sent a memo to partner sportsbooks prohibiting certain types of bets this season. The league has the authority to restrict betting types through its agreements. Going forward, bettors will not be able to include the under on the same player's statistics in parlays. The league also directed sportsbooks to not offer bets on the winner of the opening tip, players to miss specific shots, and under bets on players who are expected to play fewer than 12 minutes in a specific game.

"There's a balance between ensuring that we are removing problematic bet types but also ensuring that we don't just move activity into the illegal market," NBA executive vice president Scott Kaufman-Ross told ESPN. The league thinks the new restrictions strike the right balance.

The NBA has seen a few players wrapped up in betting legal cases. Jontay Porter, formerly of the Toronto Raptors, pleaded guilty in July 2024 to conspiracy to commit wire fraud. He admitted deliberately leaving games early to help bettors win wagers that his statistics would fall below sportsbook thresholds. The NBA banned him for life. Terry Rozier was charged in October 2025 with wire fraud and money laundering conspiracies. Prosecutors allege he tipped off associates that he would exit a March 2023 game early, enabling more than $200K in “under” bets. He has pleaded not guilty.

The impact is negative for DraftKings (DKNG) and FanDuel (FLUT) since parlay bets have higher margins or hold rates that traditional sports bets. DraftKings (DKNG) was down 1.1% in afternoon trading, while FanDuel owner Flutter Entertainment (FLUT) was up 0.1%.

data.title: SA Asks: Are neocloud stocks a buy after this week's sell-off? (Update)
data.description:
(Updated to add comments from SA analyst Yiannis Zourmpanos.)

Are neocloud stocks a buy after this week's sell-off?

Seeking Alpha analysts Yiannis Zourmpanos, Danil Sereda, Petri Dish Reports, and Carla Magliocco weigh in.

Yiannis Zourmpanos: My take after the neocloud sell-off is Nebius (NBIS) is a solid buy, IREN (IREN) a selective buy/hold, and CoreWeave (CRWV) a wait.

AI demand hasn’t broken. But CoreWeave's (CRWV) credit stress exposed the new reality: backlog isn’t enough anymore; financing, execution, and cash conversion decide who wins.

Danil Sereda: In a recent article, I compared Nebius (NBIS) and CoreWeave (CRWV) to find the future outperformer, and following the sell-off that we're seeing now in both of them, I'm not changing my opinion that Nebius (NBIS) looks superior in the long run. 

First, it's the management team. Nebius (NBIS) has a CEO who built Yandex, the biggest tech conglomerate in the CIS region, and one of the biggest in Eurasia in general. The team is very experienced, and Nebius holds a massive advantage over CoreWeave (CRWV) in terms of labor costs and flexibility. 

Second, their balance sheet remains quite strong. I know it's going to take on incremental debt in the next few years, but I like the way management structures the new debt loads and attracts money through convertibles or direct stakes from Nvidia (NVDA) and others. 

If we recall why neocloud stocks are dropping so much, we'll find that it was due to Gartner predicting that ~80% of neoclouds will evaporate by 2030. Nebius is unlikely to be one of those evaporated companies, in my opinion. Not in a today-like environment of rising demand for AI workloads and all that. 

Coming back to the main question, I'd like to answer that not all neoclouds deserve a Buy rating on the dip. Nebius (NBIS) deserves it for the reasons I listed above. CoreWeave (CRWV) doesn't, because its debt levels look extreme, and the odds of evaporating are mathematically higher. At least that's how I see the setup. 

Ex-miners such as IREN (IREN), Cipher Digital (CIFR), or Wolfspeed (WOLF) are also not Buys because they seem to lack the superior tech filling that Nebius and CoreWeave have. They're mainly just selling GPU compute, where the asset base is at risk of becoming obsolete. Neoclouds need to have SaaS-filling and tech features to give customers more offerings and make sure their workloads don't break at some point. Small ex-miners don't seem to be capable of doing that, in my opinion.

In short, I'd only go with Nebius (NBIS) on this dip and ignore all other tickers.

(Danil Sereda leads the SA investing group Beyond the Wall Investing.) 

Petri Dish Reports: The Gartner report had a big impact on market sentiment. My main argument is that we should treat AI infrastructure demand and neocloud shareholder returns as two completely different investment questions. The reality is that the industry is going to expand pretty rapidly, while some infrastructure providers struggle with financing costs, GPU depreciation, or even weak margins and dilution.

When we compare big players like CoreWeave (CRWV), Nebius (NBIS), Iren (IREN), and Applied Digital (APLD), we need to focus on three areas. 

First, who captures the economics? We have to compare their contract pricing, margins, and differentiation rather than simply relying on a player's backlog figure or projected revenue. 

Second, who can actually finance their growth sustainably? Debt obligations, cash flow, and construction costs are going to have an impact. 

Lastly, who owns assets that actually retain value? What I mean by this is that we need to distinguish GPU-dependent businesses from companies whose economics are tied to land, power, and some hefty long-term data center leases. 

Everyone realizes that choosing which company will win is the hard part here, but first we should understand that treating all neoclouds as one investment category is going to overlook some very meaningful differences in their business models and financing risks.

Carla Magliocco: The market is going through a panic spiral in AI similar to the one we saw in the last week of July. And where there's panic, buy! I took the opportunity to expand my position in Nebius (NBIS).

It's true that this time the economic factors are more deteriorated than in July, especially because taking on debt for big investments has become more expensive. All equities are suffering in this context, and AI is suffering as well. But the cost of debt hits neoclouds such as Nebius (NBIS), CoreWeave (CRWV), Hut 8 (HUT), and IREN (IREN) harder, because their growth models depend on large expenditures by hyperscalers. Remember, however, that this context calls into question the financing capacity, not the development nor the profitability of AI.

That’s why now is the time to stay calm and put any available liquidity, big or small, to work. And those who have no more liquidity, just hold your position. Neoclouds offer a key and highly specialized service for AI hardware: computing power. If you have doubts about this thesis, where the expected returns in this bottleneck are huge, selling wouldn’t be the best alternative.

data.title: Shell to sell French fuel stations to DCC Energy - Reuters
data.description:
Shell (SHEL) has reached a deal with Ireland-based DCC Energy for the proposed ​sale of its network of fuel retail stations and related ‌transport fuel services in France, Reuters reported Friday, without providing financial details.

A deal has not been finalized, ​although completion is expected in Q2 2027, subject ​to consultation with employee representatives, according to the report, which also said the transaction would include ~70 sites, eight LNG installations, and the transfer of 35 employees.

DCC Energy reportedly would operate the stations under a long-term Shell (SHEL) brand license, but Shell's core fuel supply operations would be excluded, ​meaning the ⁠buyer would source its fuel independently.

DCC Energy serves millions of customers across the industrial and public sectors and delivers off-grid energy solutions, led by liquid gas, the company's website ​said.

data.title: Sandpiper comes out against H&R's proposed Go REIT deal
data.description:
Sandpiper Group, which owns about 1% of outstanding H&R Real Estate Investment Trust (HR.UN:CA) (HRUFF), is against H&R's planned Go Residential REIT (GO.U:CA) (GO.U) deal.

"The central question is whether this particular transaction delivers compelling value to H&R's public unitholders on terms that are transparent, balanced, and in our best interests. We have serious concerns that it does not," said Samir Manji, founder and CEO of Sandpiper Group, in a statement on Friday. "That is why Sandpiper intends to vote AGAINST the Transaction."

Sandpiper joins a chorus of other investors who have come out against the deal, including RBC Global Asset Management and  Mill Pond last week.

In August, H&R REIT agreed to be acquired by Go Residential and a consortium including Blackstone (BX), Crestpoint, PSP Investments, and a company controlled by members of the family of H&R CEO Tom Hofstedter in a deal valued at ~C$6.7B.

data.title: Investors are flocking to leveraged semiconductor ETFs
data.description:
The Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF (SOXL) has seen more than $3.8B in inflows this week so far and is on track for its largest weekly intake on record.

The SOXL ETF has now had three consecutive weeks of inflows, the longest streak since May. Its previous record for weekly inflow was more than $3.1B in June.

The ETF, however, is down 7.2% on midday trade on Friday, down almost 25% this week, and down 35% over the past seven trading days.

 

 

 

On the other hand, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) posted more than $430M in inflows so far this week and is on track for its biggest weekly inflow since the beginning of September. The SMH ETF is down 8% this week.

In addition, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX)—also down about 9% this week—has attracted more than $574M in inflows and is on pace for its second-largest weekly intake since August.

data.title: Viatris, Opus granted FDA label expansion for Ryzumvi in presbyopia
data.description:
Opus Genetics (IRD) on Friday announced that the U.S. FDA has granted a label expansion for Ryzumvi, an eye care solution it markets with Viatris (VTRS), allowing its use in adults with presbyopia, an age-related condition characterized by loss of clear close-up vision.

The treatment, also known as phentolamine ophthalmic solution, was previously available in the U.S. for patients aged three years and older with pharmacologically induced mydriasis (dilated pupils).

The approval comes after the FDA accepted the company’s supplemental New Drug Application for Ryzumvi in presbyopia earlier this year, granting October 17 as the target action date.

The sNDA is backed by data from two pivotal Phase 3 trials, VEGA-2 and VEGA-3, which met their primary and all key secondary efficacy endpoints with a favorable safety profile for phentolamine ophthalmic solution.

Its approval triggers a milestone payment to Opus (IRD) from Viatris (VTRS). The companies reached a license and collaboration agreement in 2022 to market the PS treatment in the U.S. and several other overseas markets.

data.title: M&T forecasts $1.83B-$1.85B in Q4 taxable-equivalent NII while targeting 10%-10.25% CET1
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: M&T Bank (MTB) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "Diluted GAAP earnings per share were $5.04 compared to $5.32 in the prior quarter" (Senior EVP & CFO Daryl Bible).
  • "Loan growth remained solid and deposit growth more than funded the increase, allowing us to reduce our reliance on short-term borrowings while maintaining strong net interest margin" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • "Our focus on capital generation and preservation is also reflected in our decision to transfer $8.3 billion of residential mortgage-backed securities from available for sale to held to maturity" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • "Taxable equivalent net interest income was $1.8 billion, largely unchanged from the linked quarter" and "net interest margin was 3.65%, down 5 basis points from the prior quarter" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • "Average loans held for investment increased $2.6 billion or 2% to $143.3 billion" with growth "driven by commercial real estate and consumer" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • "Noninterest expenses for the quarter were $1.39 billion, an increase of $44 million from the prior quarter" and "our efficiency ratio was 54.4% in the third quarter, up from 52.8% in the linked quarter" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).

Outlook

  • "We expect taxable equivalent NII to be $1.83 billion to $1.85 billion and net interest margin to be in the mid-3.60s" and "our forecast reflects one rate hike in December" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • "We expect modest loan growth with average loans of $145 billion to $146 billion" and "average deposits are expected to increase to $169 billion to $170 billion" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • "Our outlook for the fourth quarter noninterest income is $710 million to $730 million" and "fourth quarter expenses, including intangible amortization, are expected to be $1.39 billion to $1.41 billion" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • "Net charge-offs for the fourth quarter are expected to be 35 to 40 basis points" and "we plan to continue to operate with a CET1 ratio of 10% to 10.25% for the remainder of the year" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).

Financial Results

  • "Net income was $775 million compared to $818 million in the linked quarter" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • "Average total deposits rose $3.3 billion to $166.8 billion" and "the deposit growth allowed us to reduce our reliance on borrowings with average short-term borrowing decreasing by $2.8 billion to $5.2 billion" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • "Mortgage banking revenues increased $25 million to $152 million" and "the primary driver was residential mortgage, which increased $23 million to $119 million from higher servicing fee income, reflecting $63 billion of subservicing balances added in June" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • "Criticized loans increased $245 million to $6.1 billion" and "nonaccrual loans increased $90 million to $1.3 billion" with the increase "mostly related to office and assisted living credits" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • "Net charge-offs for the quarter totaled $127 million or 35 basis points" and "in the third quarter, we recorded a provision for credit losses of $135 million" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • "The unrealized pretax loss on the available for sale portfolio was $745 million" and "M&T estimates its LCR at quarter end was 107%" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).

Q&A

  • Daniel Tamayo, Raymond James: "Is there any benefit left from this mix shift?" and "how much of that came from -- was impacted by the rate hike in September?" Senior EVP & CFO Bible: "our deposit costs were up 10 basis points quarter-over-quarter" and "4 basis points of that increase was really attributable to time deposits" tied to "a 4.05% rate on those CDs"; he added, "I feel very optimistic on the outlook for net interest income and net interest margin."
  • Bill Young, TD Cowen: asked about "updated thoughts" on CRE growth amid "evolving higher rate environment." Senior EVP & CFO Bible: "Higher rates just by definition, is going to make it more challenging" but "we still feel confident we're going to be able to grow probably maybe mid-single digit, plus or minus."
  • Bill Young, TD Cowen: asked whether criticized assets could stabilize. Senior EVP & CFO Bible: "if rates stay higher, that could put pressure on debt service coverage ratios" and "you might see a little creep in the criticized side."
  • Eugene Sweeney, Evercore ISI: asked about an auto-leasing criticized credit and whether it was broader. Senior EVP & CFO Bible: "We believe it was idiosyncratic" and "we think [nonaccrual] is going to be flat to up a little bit as well."
  • Ryan Kenny, Morgan Stanley: asked how higher rates impact fees; Senior EVP & CFO Bible: "higher interest rates on the yield curve is definitely going to slow down our residential mortgage business" while subservicing can be "more countercyclical"; he added, "trying to get the fee revenue up into the 30s would be a great objective for us to achieve."
  • Ryan Kenny, Morgan Stanley: asked on M&A appetite. Senior EVP & CFO Bible: "There's nothing imminent" but "we're still actively talking to a lot of people in our footprint" and emphasized the "deposit franchise" as "one of the most important things we look at."
  • David Chiaverini, Jefferies: asked why C&I was muted. Senior EVP & CFO Bible: "What offset us was seasonally, dealer commercial services" and "owner-occupied"; he said, "our outlook, though, for C&I is very optimistic and good."
  • Christopher O'Connell, KBW: asked about buybacks amid Basel III. Senior EVP & CFO Bible: "we first want to get the rules out there" and cited Basel III, tailoring, and liquidity; he added, "rating agencies, we don't want to get downgraded."
  • Gerard Cassidy, RBC: asked about GenAI agents moving deposits. Senior EVP & CFO Bible: "we aren't really seeing much impact of actually money being moved out or anything yet" and "I think it's going to take time for people to get comfortable."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were slightly negative to neutral, centering on deposit-cost drivers, sustainability of CRE growth in higher rates, criticized/nonaccrual trajectory, and potential constraints from Basel III and rating agencies.
  • Management was slightly positive, repeatedly using confidence language including "we feel confident," "we're very optimistic," and "I feel very comfortable where we're operating," while acknowledging pressure points like "higher funding costs" and potential "creep" in criticized loans.
  • Versus last quarter’s emphasis on record metrics and improving credit, the tone shifted toward protecting capital (AFS-to-HTM move) and managing higher-rate second-order effects, with analysts probing deposit competition and credit normalization more directly.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Prepared remarks moved from Q2’s "highest quarterly diluted earnings per share in M&T's history" to Q3’s sequential decline in GAAP EPS and net income (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • Net interest margin shifted from Q2 "3.70% unchanged from the prior quarter" to Q3 "3.65%, down 5 basis points" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • Funding discussion shifted from Q2 average deposits declining (with end-of-period strength highlighted) to Q3 average deposits rising $3.3 billion alongside a $2.8 billion reduction in average short-term borrowings (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • Credit commentary shifted from Q2 criticized commercial loans declining and nonaccrual decreasing to Q3 criticized and nonaccrual increasing, with specific mention of "office and assisted living credits" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).

Risks and Concerns

  • "If rates stay higher, that could put pressure on debt service coverage ratios" with potential for criticized-loan "creep" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • "The unrealized pretax loss on the available for sale portfolio was $745 million" and management framed the $8.3 billion AFS-to-HTM transfer as protecting "tangible capital" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).
  • Expenses included items tied to "higher software maintenance, enhancements to our technology infrastructure" and "Visa-related litigation obligations" (Senior EVP & CFO Bible).

Final Takeaway

Management characterized Q3 as a quarter where deposit growth funded loan growth and reduced short-term borrowings, while capital actions—including transferring $8.3 billion of RMBS to HTM—were positioned as tangible-capital protection ahead of potential regulatory changes. For Q4, management guided taxable-equivalent NII of $1.83 billion to $1.85 billion, net interest margin in the mid-3.60s, and continued balance-sheet growth, alongside net charge-offs of 35 to 40 basis points and a CET1 operating range of 10% to 10.25%, while acknowledging higher-rate pressure on certain fee lines and potential credit migration in a prolonged higher-rate environment.

data.title: Apple faces risk to dominance in UK tap-to-pay market - report
data.description:
Apple (AAPL) is said to be preparing for a legal fight with a U.K. regulator with a view to protect its dominance in the country's tap-to-pay market, the Financial Times reported.

The U.K. Competition and Markets Authority is set to publish proposals for a consultation next week, which is related to making the iPhone maker open up its digital wallet technology to rival payment providers, several people familiar with the matter told the FT.

The consultation is expected to argue on whether Apple exercises unfair power over the U.K.'s tap-to-pay market and recommend changes to the iPhone's operating system, the sources reportedly said.

Apple is likely to legally challenge the decision, two people briefed on the matter told the newspaper.

The regulatory action, if successful, could be a coup for fintechs such as PayPal (PYPL), Revolut (REVOLUT), and Monzo, as well as traditional banks, the report published on Friday noted.

data.title: Alcoa rallies after posting higher Q3 profit, seeing strong aluminum fundamentals
data.description:
Alcoa (AA) rose 5.8% in Friday's trading after reporting Q3 adjusted earnings that easily beat analyst expectations, helped by higher aluminum production and prices.

Q3 GAAP earnings more than doubled to $483M, or $1.81/share, from $232M, or $0.88/share, in the year-earlier quarter, and revenues rose 24% Y/Y to $3.7B but came in slightly below Wall Street estimates; adjusted EBITDA jumped to $789M from $270M a year ago.

Q3 aluminum production rose 12% Y/Y to 649K metric tons, aluminum shipments increased 13% to 693K tons, and the average realized third-party price for aluminum surged 34% to $4,527/metric ton.

Q3 alumina production edged up 0.6% Y/Y to 2.47M tons, alumina third-party shipments fell 25% to 1.65M tons, and the average realized third-party price for alumina slipped 6.4% Y/Y to $353/ton.

For the full year, Alcoa (AA) reiterated its forecasts for aluminum production of 2.4M-2.6M metric tons, aluminum shipments of 2.6M-2.8M tons, alumina production of 9.5M-9.6M tons, and alumina shipments of 11.5M-11.6M tons.

Aluminum prices have moderated from their recent highs, but pricing remains supported by constructive market fundamentals, CEO Bill Oplinger said on the company's earnings conference call.

"On the supply side, production is gradually recovering as Middle East smelters restart and Indonesian capacity ramps up," although the timing of a full recovery to levels preceding pre-war production levels in the Middle East remains uncertain, Oplinger said.

"Global aluminum inventories remain historically low at ~42 days of consumption, leaving the market with limited capacity to absorb further supply disruptions or stronger-than-expected demand," the CEO said.

Alcoa (AA) CFO Molly Beerman said the company believes the momentum displayed in the recent quarter will continue through the end of the year.

"We are expecting higher production and shipments in both [the aluminum and alumina] segments as improved refining system stability is maintained and the smelting portfolio continues to deliver productivity through incremental output and cost discipline," Beerman said on the call.

"While we expect some higher direct input costs from elevated market prices and planned maintenance to support continued operational stability, the underlying performance remains very strong headed into the final quarter of the year."
